workload.name: Burst queue
workload.description: A burst of 15 identical jobs per runner, all queued at the same instant, each holding its runner for 60 seconds. Since 4 Oct 2026 each RunsOn job requests its own label (runs-on=<run id>-<runner id>-<iteration>), so a RunsOn runner launched for one job can no longer be taken by a sibling; before, a runner missing from a burst left one job waiting for RunsOn to retry, minutes later. Queue time shows how fast a provider absorbs a spike: how quickly it scales, and the concurrency limits of the plan this account is on. Runs on its own, never alongside another suite, in shards of one runner per provider, one shard after another (a provider's x64 and arm64 runners never share a shard, since some providers cap concurrency per account).
workload.shards: one runner per provider per shard (a provider's x64 and arm64 runners in different shards)

runners.label: runs-on={run_id},family=m9g.2xlarge,image=ubuntu26-full-arm64,ssh=false,retry=false,env=demo,extras=tmpfs
runners.note: Graviton on m9g.2xlarge with /tmp, /home/runner and /var/lib/docker in memory (extras=tmpfs): the arm64 counterpart of the x64 tmpfs runners.

suiteNotes.docker: With tmpfs, /var/lib/docker lives in RAM: a PostHog image build outgrows the 32 GB this machine shares between the tmpfs and the build itself, and the runner loses contact mid-build (out of memory).

suiteSkips.docker: Not run: needs more than 32 GB of RAM with tmpfs, where Docker's data root lives in RAM; PostHog's layers plus the build's own memory exceeded it and the runner was shut down mid-build. The 64 GB tmpfs runner builds it.
